entries.text: Max Nightriver and Naomi met Baroness Serenola in Driftmere, where she revealed that a mining expedition in Wendhope had vanished and that House Nightriver had ignored her letters. Naomi eagerly joined Max's party, and they went to the Minotaur's Tusk, where the survivor Garreth described tunnels that moved like living things and something ancient breathing in the dark. The scene carried an ominous, tense tone as the party prepared to investigate the mine.

Garreth told Max Nightriver and the party that his crew vanished on level three of the North shaft after the walls pulsed and the tunnel sealed behind them. At the tavern, an old dwarf warned that Filwern's silence in Driftmere meant something else had awakened, and Max ordered Belle, Dalan, and Naomi to gear up for a descent at first light. The party entered the mine, and in a vast carved hall, a pale, eyeless figure in a miner's tunic emerged from a side tunnel with three shambling shapes, claiming Garreth's crew now belonged to it.

Dalan opened fire on the undead miners, warning the group to aim for the head, while Belle charged in with Cleaver and Naomi guarded her with Nispelheim's fiery blade. Max Nightriver directed the formation, killed the eyeless leader with fire, and found no crew badges on the bodies. A deeper voice taunted the Nightriver blood, and the party descended to the second level, where a black-armored figure with a glowing yellow eye awaited them in a vast cavern.

The party advanced down a twisting tunnel where the walls closed in, damp and smelling of wet stone and old blood. The heavy breathing they had followed changed into rhythmic metal grinding, and a yellow light flickered at the bend ahead. Dalan drew his bow and whispered that something was waiting for them, noting the sound of metal and that the light was not a lantern.

Max Nightriver dimmed the lantern and crept toward the bend, directing Belle to wait for his signal and Dalan to aim at the yellow light. Belle gripped Cleaver in tense silence, coiled and ready, while Dalan pressed against the tunnel wall with his bow drawn and whispered that he was ready. The moment was taut with anticipation as the three prepared to strike.

The party descended into the mine tunnels and defeated a scrap-and-bone creature with exposed muscle, rusted metal, and a glowing chest cavity, using Belle's cleaver strike, Dalan's arrow, Max's fire, and Naomi's Crescent Slash. After the fight, Max found Riyo hiding in a side passage and invited her to join them despite her not being part of their Guild, and she agreed. Deeper in the tunnels, Dalan read ancient carvings warning that the floors were domains ruled by Floor Bosses awaiting an "ascension," with the name "Tzarak" carved at the end.

Max Nightriver and his companions descended through the mine's lower floors, following Riyo past ancient carvings that spoke of an ascension tied to the name Tzarak. At a ledge overlooking a vast, breathing darkness, they found an old lift and a sealed stone wall covered in glowing glyphs, while something began climbing the chain from below. The tone was tense and foreboding as the party confronted the hungry, nameless presence awaiting them.

Max Nightriver ordered Dalan to read the glyphs on a seal and reveal what was locked behind it and its true name. Dalan found the language older than dwarven and shifting under his gaze, and determined the seal held back the Unspoken Breath, with the word Tzarak repeated below, revealing that the seal kept Tzarak from ascending. The tone was tense and ominous.

Belle realized they stood before the cage of the very creature they sought as metallic scraping echoed from the chain below. Fearing Tzarak was climbing up to free itself, she readied Cleaver and vowed to bury it in stone.
Past the shattered seal lies a freezing cavern of translucent ice-like walls with thousands of frozen figures suspended inside and a black glass floor.
A vast unblinking yellow eye pulses a mile across the frozen expanse and fixes on the party.
Riyo noted that healing the seal only cut the thing below off, it did not remove it.
Belle backed Max's decision to break the seal and kill what is below.

The party confronted a gaunt, robed creature that climbed the lift chain and mimicked Riyo's voice, demanding the seal be broken so Tzarak could ascend. Belle cut the creature down while Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering of bread, salt, and a candle, which healed the seal, but Max then shattered it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. They emerged into a frozen, glass-floored cavern filled with suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened in the darkness and fixed on them.
Riyo confirmed that sealing the wall only cuts the thing below off; it still exists.
The party stands on a mirror-black glass floor in a frozen cavern, facing a vast unblinking yellow eye a mile away.
Belle is eager for the coming fight, drawing on her rage while staying clear-headed and ready for the first opening.

The frozen shapes in the ice-like walls were victims held by the Devourer's spell; killing it released them into dust rather than saving them alive.
The party emerged from the mines at sunset and found Baroness Serenola waiting outside her manor in Driftmere, demanding to know if the missing are still there.
Riyo, pale but steady after the fight, confirmed the party freed the trapped shapes and quietly acknowledged Max's victory.

Dalan determined the seal kept Tzarak from ascending, and Riyo revealed that Tzarak was not a person but a key made of shadow and hunger, and that the seal held it out rather than in. When a gaunt, robed creature climbed the lift chain mimicking Riyo's voice and demanding the seal be broken, Belle cut it down while Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering that healed the seal, only to shatter it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. They emerged into a frozen, glass-floored cavern filled with suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened in the darkness and fixed on them, leaving Serenola's missing people still unfound and the question of whether the Devourer's death dissolved them or saved them unresolved.

arcs.summary: The party descended into the mine tunnels, where they defeated a scrap-and-bone creature and Max Nightriver invited Riyo, a non-Guild fighter, to join them, then learned from ancient carvings that the floors were domains of Floor Bosses awaiting an "ascension" tied to the name Tzarak. At a ledge above a breathing darkness, Dalan read a glyph-seal older than dwarven and determined it held back the Unspoken Breath and kept Tzarak from ascending, while Riyo revealed that Tzarak was not a person but a key made of shadow and hunger, and that the seal held it out rather than in. A gaunt, robed creature climbed the lift chain mimicking Riyo's voice and demanded the seal be broken so the key could ascend, and Belle cut it down as Max performed a Driftmere shrine offering of bread, salt, and a candle that healed the seal. Max then shattered the seal with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below, and the party emerged into a frozen, glass-floored cavern of suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened in the darkness and fixed on them, leaving the wider consequences of breaking Filwern's seal and killing the creature yet to be seen.

arcs.text: The three letters Serenola sent to House Nightriver were never seen by Max — who intercepted or discarded them, and why.
Max intends to tell Garreth what happened to the crew in person.
Who intercepted or discarded Serenola's three letters to House Nightriver, and why — Serenola now openly questions whether the house knew and did not care.
Max has sworn to Serenola to find out whether House Nightriver received and discarded her three letters, and she will hold him to it.
A grieving townsfolk woman whose son died in the mine is approaching the party for answers.
The grieving townsfolk mother whose son died in the mine now knows the party killed the thing that took him — whether she accepts their account or demands more remains open.
Max has been summoned to his father's study at the Nightriver estate — what Lord Javon wants is unknown.
The party must return to the Aegis City Guild Hall to claim their B-rank promotion badge and rewards.
arcs.summary: Max Nightriver ordered Dalan to read the glyphs on a seal, which revealed it held back the Unspoken Breath and kept Tzarak from ascending, and when a gaunt robed creature climbed the lift chain demanding the seal be broken, Belle cut it down while Max made a Driftmere shrine offering of bread, salt, and a candle that healed the seal before he shattered it with Nightriver fire to reach the miners below. Beyond the seal the party entered a frozen, glass-floored cavern filled with suspended figures, where a vast yellow eye opened and fixed on them, and they crossed the black glass to confront it: Max blinded it with fire, Dalan shot its eye-spot, Belle struck with Cleaver, and Max drove a lance of flame into the wound, killing the creature and freeing the suspended souls as Riyo confirmed she was unharmed and the breathing had stopped. The party climbed back to Driftmere, where Baroness Serenola received the news that the crew was gone but the creature was dead, and when Max revealed he had never seen the three letters she sent to House Nightriver, her tone turned cold and accusing as a grieving townswoman approached asking about the mine. Belle and Dalan told the woman they had killed the creature that took the missing people, though they could not bring themselves to say the victims had dissolved into dust, and the party returned to Aegis City, where Max Nightriver's letter from Tobias confirmed their promotion to B-rank for clearing the Driftmere Mines, and at the Nightriver estate the butler greeted Max and informed him his father was in his study.

arcs.text: Baroness Serenola waits in her study to speak about House Nightriver, and Max has sworn to learn whether the house received and discarded her three letters.
The party has been promoted to B-rank and must return to the Aegis City Guild Hall to claim the badge and rewards.
Riyo's refusal of a room and her guarded vigil by the estate door — what she is hiding and why she will not settle in.
Welden is behaving strangely and refuses to explain what is troubling him.
Javon has confronted Max about letters sent to the house, holding a letter with a grain-stalk seal — what he knows about Serenola's three unanswered letters is unresolved.
Javon has admitted the estate deliberately 'handled' Serenola's letters — what that purpose was, and who ordered it, is unresolved.
Welden is in the library, jumpier than usual and refusing to explain what troubles him.
Javon suspects Max has been receiving letters he knows nothing about — who is writing to Max, and what Javon will do about it, is unresolved.
Javon's stated purpose for 'handling' Serenola's letters remains unexplained — who ordered it and why is unresolved.
Javon has set three conditions Max must meet before he will reveal the truth of the house's seals and marriages — whether Max meets them, and what the truth is, is unresolved.
The truth of the Nightriver seals and the Witch King — Max now knows the bloodline is the prison, but how to act on it, and what Javon's three conditions will reveal, is unresolved.
